name: Locate underground plant for excavators
summary: Anyone who digs in Ontario must request a locate through Ontario One Call, which sends the request to every utility with plant nearby. The utility screens each ticket against its maps, clears those with no cables in the dig area, and has a locator mark the rest with paint and flags within five business days, using contract locators for routine tickets and its own cable locators for high-voltage and complex plant. Spring and summer volumes exceed capacity, so tickets queue and late locates hold up excavators and the utility's own crews. Mismarked or missed cables lead to strikes, outages and safety incidents.

baseline.org_archetype: A municipally owned Ontario distributor with about 350,000 customers and 3,167 km of underground circuit, whose locates are mostly delivered by a contract locate provider.
baseline.notes: Covers the utility's own electrical plant only; other utilities mark their own plant on the same ticket. Describes 2019-2022, before the 2022 Bill 93 changes took full effect.

trigger: Ontario One Call transmits a locate request for a dig area that touches the utility's registered area.
end_state: The excavator has a clearance or a marked locate with a locate sheet; or a damage that followed a locate has been investigated and referred.

volume.seasonality: Lowest from December to March when the ground is frozen; rises sharply from April with the start of construction, peaks May to September, and stays high into November.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate kept (about 90,000 a year). It agrees with a search-engine excerpt of a later Hydro Ottawa rate filing reporting about 87,000 to 104,000 locates a year in 2017-2021, which could not be opened.

surge.cause: spring start of construction, when frozen-season backlog and new projects arrive together

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the organisation file describes spring and summer volumes exceeding in-house capacity.
Screening, assignment and late-date calls at about 3.5 minutes per ticket; shares the six field dispatchers with field service orders.

Author's estimate of contractor staff and billed cost per hour. A search-engine excerpt of a later Hydro Ottawa rate filing said its locates were delivered by external vendors at about $3.1M a year; the filing could not be opened (PDF), so this is not cited.
Ten cable locators do complex, high-voltage and emergency locates, about 12% of field tickets.
Do Not Proceed reviews, field audits and damage investigations.

systems.name: Ontario One Call member portal and locate management
Geographic information system (asset and network model)
Document management and engineering drawing repository
Mobile workforce management and field tablets
Contact centre telephony, IVR and call recording
Health, safety and environment incident system

resources.name: Light vehicle (pickup or van) for locators, meter technicians, inspectors and field service

steps.name: Receive locate notification from One Call
steps.description: Ontario One Call transmits each locate request whose dig area touches the utility's registered area to the utility's locate management system, with the excavator, address, dig area description, type of work and requested start date.

evidence.note: Locate requests through Ontario One Call, five business days, colour-coded marks; times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Screen ticket against plant maps
steps.description: A dispatcher opens the ticket map and the GIS underground layer side by side and decides whether the dig area is clear of the utility's cables, needs a field locate, or is an emergency. Large or vague dig areas are flagged for a call to the excavator.

error.defect_description: Ticket cleared although plant is in the dig area (map error or misread).

control.basis: Ontario Underground Infrastructure Notification System Act, 2012: members must respond to every locate request within the set time

next.condition: no plant in the dig area

evidence.note: Clear and emergency shares are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Issue desk clearance
steps.description: For tickets with no utility plant in the dig area the dispatcher sends the excavator a clearance notice by email or fax from the locate system and closes the ticket as cleared in the One Call portal.

evidence.note: Locate requests through Ontario One Call, five business days, colour-coded marks; times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Assign ticket to a locator
steps.description: The dispatcher bundles tickets by area and due date and assigns routine ones to the contract locate provider and complex ones (high-voltage duct banks, downtown network, large projects) to the utility's own cable locators. Tickets that cannot be done by the due date are flagged.

evidence.note: In-house share sized to ten cable locators; the rest goes to contract locators.

steps.name: Agree a later date with the excavator
steps.description: When the locate cannot be done by the due date the dispatcher calls the excavator to agree a new date or a partial locate for the first phase of work, and records the agreement on the ticket to avoid a late-locate complaint.

evidence.note: Late locates were widespread in Ontario (up to 85% late, 49% of tickets over 15 days per One Call data); share here is the author's estimate for a city with a dedicated contractor.

steps.name: Contract locator drives to site
steps.description: When the ticket reaches the top of the contractor's route, a contract locator drives to the dig site, usually doing several tickets in one neighbourhood in a day.

evidence.note: Queue time before the visit stands for contractor capacity, longest in the spring and summer peak.

steps.name: Locate and mark cables
steps.description: The locator connects a transmitter to the cable or uses induction, traces the cable with a receiver across the dig area, compares the signal with the utility's map, and marks the route with red paint and flags. Unclear dig areas or blocked access stop the locate.

error.defect_description: Cable mismarked or missed (poor signal, map error, missed service).

control.basis: Locate marking practice under CSA Z247 damage prevention guidance and the utility's locate standard (paint and flags within the locate tolerance zone)

next.condition: dig area unclear or no access

evidence.note: Locate requests through Ontario One Call, five business days, colour-coded marks; times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Contact excavator about site problems
steps.description: The locator calls the excavator about a missing white-lined area, a locked yard or a dig area too large to locate in one visit, and arranges to come back once the site is accessible.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Complete locate sheet and close ticket
steps.description: The locator fills in the locate sheet with a sketch, measurements from fixed features and validity period, leaves it at the site or emails it to the excavator, and closes the ticket as located in the locate system.

evidence.note: Locate requests through Ontario One Call, five business days, colour-coded marks; times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Respond to emergency locate call-out
steps.description: For an emergency request (a water main break, gas leak or the utility's own cable fault) the on-call cable locator is called out and drives straight to the site, ahead of the routine queue.

evidence.note: Emergency response times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Cable locator drives to site
steps.description: A utility cable locator picks up complex tickets on the daily route (high-voltage feeders, duct banks, the downtown network, large construction projects) and drives to the site.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Locate complex plant
steps.description: The cable locator traces feeders and duct banks with transmitter and receiver, checks vault and manhole positions against the GIS and as-built drawings, and marks the routes; for crowded or high-voltage areas they mark the area where excavation needs extra care.

error.defect_description: Duct bank offset or depth misjudged.

control.basis: Locate marking practice under CSA Z247 damage prevention guidance and the utility's locate standard (paint and flags within the locate tolerance zone)

next.condition: high-voltage cable close to the dig

evidence.note: Locate requests through Ontario One Call, five business days, colour-coded marks; times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Apply Do Not Proceed notice
steps.description: Where high-voltage cables are close to the planned dig, the locator leaves a Do Not Proceed sticker or notice telling the excavator not to dig until the utility has reviewed a Request to Excavate.

control.basis: Utility Do Not Proceed procedure for excavation near high-voltage cables

evidence.note: Do Not Proceed sticker or notice near high-voltage cables; share of complex tickets is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for Request to Excavate
steps.description: The excavator fills in the utility's Request to Excavate form with contact details, locate ticket number, exact address and a description of the planned excavation and sends it in.

evidence.note: Form contents from Hydro Ottawa; excavator response time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review excavation plan and set conditions
steps.description: The field services supervisor reviews the form against the cable records, decides whether a utility standby, hand digging, hydrovac or a cable outage is needed, and calls the excavator with the conditions.

control.basis: Utility review of excavation near high-voltage cables before digging proceeds

evidence.note: Hydro Ottawa replies within 48 business hours; review time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Deliver locate and close ticket
steps.description: The cable locator or supervisor completes the locate sheet with sketch and conditions, gives it to the excavator and closes the ticket in the locate system.

evidence.note: Locate requests through Ontario One Call, five business days, colour-coded marks; times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Audit locate in the field
steps.description: The field services supervisor visits a sample of completed locates, mostly from the contractor, and checks the marks against a fresh trace and the locate sheet for accuracy and completeness. Errors are sent back for a re-mark and recorded against the contractor.

control.basis: Utility audit of contract locate quality

evidence.note: Sampling rate and error rate are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Investigate cable damage
steps.description: When an excavator strikes a cable, after the trouble crew has made it safe, the supervisor visits the site, compares the marks and locate sheet with where the cable was hit, interviews the excavator and the locator and takes photos to decide whether the locate or the digging was at fault.

evidence.note: Damage rate of a few per thousand located tickets is the author's estimate; the delay is the time between the locate and the dig.

steps.name: Record incident and refer claim
steps.description: The supervisor files the incident in the safety system and sends the investigation to legal and claims, who bill the excavator for repairs or handle a claim against the locate contractor.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Cannot meet the due date
exceptions.description: The contractor queue is too long and the dispatcher agrees a later date with the excavator.

exceptions.name: Site not ready
exceptions.description: No white-lining, locked yard or dig area too large; the locator returns later.

exceptions.name: Do Not Proceed near high-voltage cable
exceptions.description: The excavator must send a Request to Excavate and wait for the utility's conditions.

exceptions.name: Emergency locate
exceptions.description: An on-call cable locator is called out ahead of the queue.

exceptions.name: Cable strike after locate
exceptions.description: A cable is struck during excavation; the supervisor investigates whether the locate or the digging was at fault and refers the claim.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from notification to clearance or delivered locate
benchmarks.population: Locate requests at a mid-size Ontario distributor, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: about a third of tickets are cleared within a day; field locates aim at five business days (about seven calendar days) and run later in the spring and summer peak. Ontario-wide lateness (see the next benchmark) was worse, driven largely by the Toronto region.

benchmarks.unit: share of requests later than five business days (upper figure quoted)
benchmarks.population: Ontario locate requests before the 2022 reforms

evidence.note: Industry article; figure is quoted as 'as high as' and is not attributed to a named data set.

benchmarks.unit: share of tickets taking longer than 15 days
benchmarks.population: Ontario One Call data reported in 2022

evidence.note: Reported by the article from One Call data; the underlying data set was not opened.

pain_points.description: Spring and summer volumes exceed locator capacity, so tickets queue past the five-business-day deadline and excavators and the utility's own crews wait.

evidence.note: Province-wide lateness and idle-time costs reported in 2022.

pain_points.description: Map errors and poor signals lead to mismarks found only by audit or by a cable strike.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Excavation near high-voltage cables waits for a Request to Excavate and a supervisor review.

evidence.note: Up to 48 business hours for the utility's reply.

sources.title: Locates - safe digging (information for contractors)
sources.supports: Locate requests go through Ontario One Call at least five business days before digging (ten for multi-address requests); colour-coded ground markings; stay 1.5 m from marked cables and hand dig or hydrovac near them; request a re-locate when marks are unclear or expire; near high-voltage cables Hydro Ottawa places a 'Do Not Proceed' sticker or notice, the excavator completes a Request to Excavate form, and Hydro Ottawa replies within 48 business hours.

sources.title: Industry group praises crucial reforms to Ontario's utility locates system
sources.supports: Locates are legally due within five business days but 'as high as 85 per cent' of requests are late; Ontario One Call data showed 49 per cent of tickets took longer than 15 days; idle time costs about $1,000 an hour in sewer and watermain work; Bill 93 reforms (shared locates, 60-day minimum validity, dedicated locators).

assumptions: Loaded costs for utility staff are taken from the organisation file (wage times 1.40 for benefits, pension, payroll taxes and overhead); the contract locator cost is the author's estimate of contractor billing per hour.

Most field locates are done by a contract locate provider. The organisation file describes in-house locators with contractor overflow, but ten in-house locators cannot mark about 5,000 field tickets a month at over an hour each (about 38 FTE of contract locators is implied); a search excerpt of a later Hydro Ottawa rate filing (not opened) said locates were done by external vendors.
The wait before the contract locator's visit stands for the contractor's queue; it is the main source of elapsed time and is longer in the spring and summer peak than the annual triangle shows.
Damage investigations start days to weeks after the locate, when the excavation happens; those cases have long cycle times but are rare.
The five-business-day deadline is taken from Hydro Ottawa's contractor page; the statute page returned an access error.
